products.short_description: Deploy GlobalProtect Connect Before Logon (PLAP) during Hybrid Azure AD Join Windows Autopilot with Microsoft Intune — one correctly sequenced Win32 app that installs, enables, and registers Connect Before Logon and lets the Enrollment Status Page own the reboot. Ends the “unzipping” error, the missing sign-in tile, and the reboot loop. Self-guided, tested, diagnosable.
products.description:
Your Autopilot build stalls on the “unzip” error and the invisible Connect Before Logon tile — this fixes it

You moved off Always On VPN to user-initiated VPN after a security incident, but you still provision with Hybrid Azure AD Join Windows Autopilot — which needs a domain controller before the user signs in. GlobalProtect Connect Before Logon (PLAP) is the answer, but the base client installs fine while the PLAP registration intermittently fails with an “unzipping” error, reboot orchestration breaks the Enrollment Status Page, and the Connect Before Logon control never reliably shows at the Windows 11 sign-in screen. This solution makes it deployable and diagnosable: one correctly sequenced Intune Win32 app that installs GlobalProtect (5.2+), writes the PanSetup registry, waits for the GlobalProtect service, registers PLAP as SYSTEM, and returns exit code 3010 so the ESP owns the reboot — plus a log-capture runbook that turns any failed provisioning into a known cause.

Run it yourself — simpler, cheaper, and proven

You do not need a consultant. The package hands you the field-tested method as self-guided, click-by-click documentation a competent admin can follow end to end — backed by ready-to-run PowerShell.

  • Simpler — exact, ordered steps with full navigation paths; every object you create is named and reused through testing and troubleshooting.
  • Cheaper — one fixed price instead of an open meter; a comparable consulting engagement runs well into the thousands per day. Reusable on every rollout.
  • Tested — a pilot-first method (Assess → Configure → Pilot → Validate → Expand) with explicit pass/fail gates, validated on Windows 11.

What's inside

  • Solution Overview — the scenario (Always On → user-initiated VPN; hybrid Autopilot needs pre-logon DC reachability), what Connect Before Logon (CBL/PLAP) is, and the single-Win32-app delivery model (install + Prelogon=1 + portal + PanGPS.exe -registerplap + return 3010).
  • Requirements Guide — every prerequisite (Intune + Autopilot Hybrid-Join profile, ESP, Domain Join/ODJ connector, the GlobalProtect 5.2+ MSI + portal FQDN + auth method, optional PKI, the Assigned device group owned by the Intune Provisioning Client service principal, the AV/IMECache exclusion) with how to verify and how to implement each if missing.
  • Implementation Guide — exact, ordered steps with Gate A–E: build the single Win32 app (System context, detection on GP≥5.2 + Prelogon=1 + PLAP registered, return-code mapping), add it as an ESP blocking app, target the enrollment-time device group, then pilot on Windows 11, validate, and expand. Documents the two-app alternative.
  • 5 PowerShell tools — readiness discovery (incl. the group's service-principal owner check), on-device Windows 11 validation, a diagnostic log collector, fleet coverage reporting, and an enrollment-time device-group builder that sets the SP owner.
  • Testing & Troubleshooting Guides with explicit pass/fail gates and a full failure-mode matrix (the unzip 0x87D30067 error, the missing PLAP tile, reboot-loop / IME state loss, ESP hangs, Win10-vs-Win11, hybrid first-logon failures, and the empty enrollment-time group), plus field-proven Best Practices.

What you receive — every file in your download

This package is delivered as downloadable files you keep and reuse across unlimited devices — nothing is left out and nothing else is required:

  • Implementation Guide (PDF) — the complete, click-by-click solution: solution overview, requirements, step-by-step implementation, testing & validation, troubleshooting, best practices.
  • PowerShell Scripts (ZIP) — 5 ready-to-run tools (read-only discovery/validation/reporting and collection; scope-targeting defaults to a safe preview):
    • GPPLAP-Collect-Logs.ps1 — the test-window diagnostic collector: gathers IME logs, Autopilot/MDM diagnostics, and GlobalProtect PanGPS/PanGPA logs into one timestamped ZIP
    • GPPLAP-Discovery.ps1 — readiness sweep for the app, cert profile, Autopilot device groups (flags a missing Provisioning Client SP owner) and ESP blocking-app reference
    • GPPLAP-Report.ps1 — GlobalProtect PLAP install-coverage report across the Autopilot fleet
    • GPPLAP-Set-ScopeTargeting.ps1 — create/populate the Assigned Autopilot device group(s) and set the Provisioning Client SP as owner
    • GPPLAP-Validation.ps1 — confirm on THIS Windows 11 device that GlobalProtect is 5.2+, Connect Before Logon is enabled, and PLAP is registered

The repeatable way

Every solution follows the same repeatable shape, so each deployment feels familiar and low-risk — buy once, reuse the playbook for the next wave and the next project.

The bottom line

GlobalProtect Connect Before Logon installed and registered during Hybrid-Join Autopilot, with the sign-in tile present at first logon — delivered as a single sequenced app that lets ESP own the reboot, made diagnosable with a log-capture runbook, and proven on a Windows 11 pilot before you scale.

Delivered as a Word document and PDF, plus all PowerShell scripts in a single ZIP — yours to keep and reuse.
